title: Makonde Cassava and Bean Stew
localName: Mchuzi wa Muhogo na Maharage — Wamakonde
community: Makonde people of Mtwara — the great carvers of southern Tanzania
author: Mama Salima

heritage.origin: Makonde people of Mtwara and the Makonde Plateau — renowned worldwide for their wood carving
heritage.history: The Makonde (Wamakonde) people of southern Tanzania's Mtwara region are world-famous for their intricate ebony wood carvings — considered among the finest sculptural traditions in Africa. Their homeland, the Makonde Plateau, is semi-arid and cassava grows better than any other crop here. Makonde cuisine is built around cassava in every form — fresh, dried, pounded — combined with beans and peanuts for protein. The Makonde cassava and bean stew is the daily meal of the plateau.

desc: Makonde Cassava and Bean Stew — fresh cassava chunks and kidney beans simmered together with peanuts, tomatoes, and onions in the traditional Makonde style of Mtwara. Simple, nutritious, and completely local — the daily meal of the great carvers.
longDesc: Makonde cassava and bean stew reflects the Makonde Plateau's ecology — cassava grows better than any other staple in the semi-arid conditions, and beans and peanuts provide the protein. This stew is the embodiment of Makonde food wisdom: use what grows here, make it nutritious and filling, waste nothing.
ingredients: 400g fresh cassava — peeled and cut into chunks
steps: Heat oil. Cook onions until golden.
Add tomatoes. Cook 6 minutes until thick.
Cover and cook 20—25 minutes until cassava is completely tender.
Mix groundnut paste with ½ cup warm water. Add to pot.
Simmer 10 more minutes until sauce is thick and well-integrated.
chefTips: Cassava must be completely tender — test with a fork.
The groundnut paste added near the end gives the Makonde version its distinctive richness.
commonMistakes: Adding groundnut paste too early — it scorches.
cookingScience: See TZA103 for groundnut sauce science.
sustainabilityTips: Cassava is the most drought-tolerant staple crop — perfectly suited to the Makonde Plateau's semi-arid climate.
healthBenefits: Complete protein from beans and peanuts combined.
culturalNote: Makonde cassava stew is the food that sustains the great carvers of southern Tanzania — simple, filling, and made entirely from what the plateau provides. The same hands that create the world's most intricate wood sculptures prepare this honest, direct stew.
